title.narrative: Technical supervision of the safe water supply for Terra Prometida in the island of Principe, Sao Tomé and Pincipe.

description.narrative:
The proposed Water Supply project will give access to drinking water to the community of the new neighbourhood Terra Prometida, in the Island of Principe, thus contributing to improved quality in health and living standards of the said community and helping materialise a model for sustainable urbanisation in Sao Tome and Principe. Terra Prometida, a new settlement in its final phase of construction and the main social housing project ever built in the country, aims at improving the living conditions of the 133 families that make up the community currently living in Roça Sundy, in the Island of Principe. For the community, this improvement is realised as they move out from the deteriorated 'sanzalas' –the old slave quarters at the former colonial plantation farm, Roça Sundy– and obtain adequate and proper housing in Terra Prometida, through a voluntary, participatory, and inclusive process, based on human rights. With the aim of promoting harmony between people and nature, Terra Prometida –a collaboration that has brought together HBD-TI, UN-Habitat, and the Regional Government of Principe– is oriented towards achieving the environmental and social sustainability of the new neighbourhood as well as creating and promoting economic and development opportunities for its inhabitants. For this purpose, the proposed drinking water supply project has been designed to achieve the highest level of sustainability possible in the Principe context, thus also contributing to fulfil the commitment of the country towards the Sustainable Development Goals, in particular SDG 6 and SDG 11. Up to date, all 133 houses have already been constructed, and the electricity supply for houses and streetlights has been provided by the Government. The implementation of the drinking water supply project will allow beneficiary families to move into the new houses and will foster the construction of a kindergarten, a health centre, and basic roadworks and drainage, thus creating the basic conditions for a successful finalisation of the Terra Prometida project. To increase the sustainability of the project, the water supply system for Terra Prometida has two components: a) a domestic rainwater-harvesting system in each house –to service WCs, showers, and laundries, already in its final construction phase; and b) a drinking water system, to which this proposal refers to, that includes two taps in each house, one in the kitchen and one in the toilet. Thus, the consumption of treated water gets reduced, guaranteeing more sustainability. This project proposal will include the drinking water system’s sourcing, piping, treatment, and distribution to the individual houses. Sustainability and maintenance of the water supply system will be secured through the engagement of EMAE, the national company for water and energy. This system has been designed to serve the current target population and its expected growth over the next 25 years. Additionally, it is foreseen that acceptable arrangements can be put in place by project partners to populate Terra Prometida as soon as possible, as time is the main concern for a successful project implementation.
Main Accomplishment: Sustainable Safe Water Supply System for Terra Prometida.
Main Results: - Potable water supply for 133 new houses and 3 public buildings (primary school, kindergarten and health post); - Water captation system; - Water treatment plant; - Water piping and domestic distribution; - Estimated number of beneficiaries: 511 people from Roça Sundy community, including 248 children. 49 school kids from other communities (Ponta do Sol, Oqué Daniel) Total = 560 direct beneficiaries.
